When you are not sure, or you forgot what an icon does, press it and hold until a window pops up with an explanation. Some icons are not active in the free version. You will find the app settings on the Profile page. Enjoy Verbigem!

Two people, one phone. Side A speaks or types in their language, side B hears and reads the translation in theirs. Tap the microphone to speak, or type below and press the arrow. Nothing here is saved and nothing ever leaves this device — the conversation is completely private.

Take a photo of a sign, menu or label — Verbigem reads the text straight off the image, offline, and translates it. Pick a picture from the gallery or shoot a new one, mark the area you want read, then translate. The picture itself never leaves your phone.

Chat is your inbox of translated conversations with friends. Open a thread to read and write — each of you sees the messages in your own language. Use the search field to find words inside your messages. Long-press any icon to read what it does.

You write in your language, your friend reads in theirs — Verbigem translates every message both ways. Tap the paper clip for a photo, the microphone to dictate, the arrow to send. Long-press a message for more options such as quote, show original or delete.

Four ways to reach people: Friends are people you already connected with, Invites are requests waiting for your answer, Phone looks them up in your address book, and External lets you write to someone through another app. Long-press any icon to read what it does.

Everything about your account and the way the app looks lives here: your nickname, the interface language, your two conversation languages, your account status and wallet, your phone number, the theme, your QR code and the privacy policy. Long-press any icon to read what it does.

Settings that live only on your device for this one friend: a private alias (nobody else sees it), the language their incoming messages are translated into, pin to keep the thread at the top, mute to silence notifications, and block to drop their messages. Long-press any control for details.
Go back to the previous screen.
Keep this chat at the top of your inbox so it is always easy to find.
Silence notifications from this contact. Messages still arrive, but your phone will not buzz.
Drop every incoming message from this contact — you will not see them, and they will not know.
Hide the whole conversation from your inbox. The other side keeps it. You can bring it back later from this screen.
The language you speak or paste in. Tap to pick it from the list. Whatever you type or say in the box below is understood as this language.
The language you want to get out. Tap to pick it. The translation, and anything read aloud, comes back in this language.
Flips the two languages around in one tap. Handy when the conversation turns and you start translating the other way. Text already in the box stays where it is.
Type here, or press and hold the microphone and speak — the words land in this box. The X on the right clears the field. You can also bring text in from a photo with the camera buttons.
Clears the box so you can start a fresh sentence. It does not touch your translation history.
Runs the engine you picked above and shows the result underneath. It stays greyed out until there is something in the box. If the model is missing, the app offers to download it once.

Tap to start and stop dictation. Speak clearly, in the source language you picked; recognised words appear in the box and you can correct them before translating. The first tap asks for microphone permission.
Opens Camera OCR: take a picture of a sign, menu or label and Verbigem turns the printed text into editable text, then translates it. Works offline, free of charge.
The Pro camera adds sharper recognition for difficult images: handwriting, low light and long documents. It stays locked in the free version — the standard camera button next to it is free.

The quick one. A compact model (about 440 MB) that runs entirely on your phone, so it needs no internet and answers almost immediately. Best for everyday sentences and for travelling. It is free and it is the default. Pick it when you want an answer right now.

The careful one. A much larger model (about 1.1 GB) that takes noticeably longer but handles long, formal or ambiguous sentences far better — contracts, instructions, anything where the exact wording matters. It also runs offline. Pro feature: free users see a padlock. Download it once over Wi-Fi.

Runs both local models on the same text and shows you the two results one under the other, so you can pick the better wording. Roughly twice the waiting time. Pro feature. Great when you are translating something you are about to send out and want to be sure.

Sends the text to a translation service on the internet and gets a very high quality result back — often the best of the four. It needs a working connection and uses a little of your API wallet. Pro feature. Use it when accuracy matters most and you are online.
The main screen: pick two languages, type or speak, translate.
Two people, one phone — speak or type and each side hears their own language.
Your inbox of translated conversations with friends.
Friends, invitations, people from your address book and external threads.
Your account, languages, theme, QR code and privacy settings.
Camera OCR — turn printed text on a sign or a menu into editable text and translate it.
Puts the text on your clipboard so you can paste it anywhere — into a message, a note, another app. Nothing is uploaded; the copy lives only on your phone.
Opens the Android share sheet and hands the text to whichever app you pick — WhatsApp, e-mail, SMS. The text leaves your phone only once you confirm the target app.
Reads the text aloud with the voice built into your phone. Works offline, in the target language. The quality is whatever Android provides — the Pro button next to it sounds more natural.
Reads the text aloud with a high-quality online voice — clearer and more natural than the built-in one. It needs a connection and uses a little of your API wallet. Locked in the free version.
Removes this entry. In history it deletes the saved translation from this phone for good; in the result card it only clears the result from the screen — the history entry stays.

The translation. The icons on top act on this text: copy, share, read aloud, read aloud Pro and clear. With the “both” engine you get two cards — the fast result first, the accurate one below it, labelled.
A translation you made earlier, kept on this phone. Tap the icons to copy, share, read it aloud or delete it. Long-press any icon to find out what it does. History is private to you.
Flips which language is spoken and which is translated, so the other person can answer. Use it whenever the turn passes to the other side.

Tap once to start listening, tap again to stop. What you said is recognised, translated, shown in the bubble and read aloud in the other language. Pass the phone to the other person when it is their turn.
Sends the text from the box below as the current side — it is translated, shown in the bubble and spoken aloud. Use it in noisy places where the microphone struggles.
Takes a new picture with the camera. Hold the phone steady and fill the frame with the text you want read. The picture stays on your device.
Picks an existing picture from your gallery — handy for screenshots, photos you already took or documents.
The text recognised from the picture appears here and you can correct it by hand before translating. Once you edit it yourself, it is not recognised again.
Translates the recognised text with the engine chosen on the Translator screen and shows the result below, ready to copy or read aloud.
Point the camera at a friend\'s Verbigem QR code to open their card and add them straight away. Your own code is on the Profile page.
Type a nickname or an e-mail address to find a person. Two characters is enough to start. Nothing is searched online until you confirm.
People you have already connected with. Tap one to open a chat; long-press for the contact card with language, pin, mute and block.
Requests waiting for your answer — from people who want to be your friend and from people you invited. Accept or decline here.
Looks through the address book on your phone and shows who already uses Verbigem. Only scrambled one-way codes of the numbers are sent for matching, never the numbers themselves.
Reads your address book and shows which of your friends already use Verbigem. Only scrambled one-way codes of the numbers are sent for matching — never the numbers themselves.
Opens a .vcf file from your device and adds the people inside as Verbigem contacts you can message right away. The file is read locally and never uploaded.
Write to somebody who has no Verbigem — through SMS, e-mail, WhatsApp and so on. Verbigem translates your message and hands it over; nothing comes back into the app.
Jumps to Contacts, where you pick the person you want to write to.
Searches the text of your messages. At least three characters are needed, and it matches the beginning of a message.
One conversation. Tap to open it and read and write. Long-press the row for the contact card with language, pin, mute, block and delete.
Dictate your message instead of typing. Tap once to start, once to stop; the recognised words land in the box so you can fix them before sending.
Attaches a picture from the gallery. It travels with the conversation and your friend can open it full screen.
Write your message here, in your own language — your friend reads it in theirs. The arrow on the right sends it.
Sends the message. It is translated for your friend on the way out, and their replies are translated for you on the way in.
A message in the thread. You always read it in your own language. Long-press it for more: show the original wording, quote it, read it aloud, translate it now, or delete it.
The name your friends see. It can be anything — it does not have to be your real name. Press Save after changing it.
Changes the language of the whole interface. It applies immediately; the languages of your translations are not affected.
Your two default languages for Conversation and for translating chats. Set the one you speak and the one you want to hear.
Shows whether you are on the free plan or Pro, and how much credit is left in your API wallet. The wallet pays for the online engine and the Pro voice.
Your phone number, used only so friends who already have it can find you. Confirming sends one SMS code; the number itself stays on your phone.
Changes the colours and the mood of the app: Calm, Sharp or Playful, each with a day and a night version.
Your personal code. Let a friend scan it — or share the link — and their app opens your card with an Add friend button.
Signs you out of this device. Your translations and chat history stay on the phone; sign in again to sync.
Opens our published privacy policy in your browser. We never read your messages — they are translated on your device and stay there.
Closes this conversation and returns to your list of chats.
Your personal code. Another Verbigem user scans it to open your contact card with an Add friend button — no typing or searching needed.
Copies your profile link to the clipboard so you can share it through any app.
Adds your phone number so friends who already have it can find you. Confirming sends one SMS code; the number itself stays on your phone and is never uploaded.
Skips verification. Chat still works, but nobody with your number in their contacts will be able to find you. You can verify later from Profile.
Best quality ~2.9 GB — the largest local model, several times slower.

The heavyweight. A 7-billion-parameter model (about 2.9 GB), roughly four times the size of Accurate, so it is clearly slower: a long sentence takes several seconds even on a fast phone. In exchange it handles idioms, word order and rare languages better than either 1.8B model. Runs offline. Pro feature, and it needs a phone with at least 6 GB of RAM and 3.5 GB of free space; on weaker devices the icon stays hidden. Download it once over Wi-Fi.

Force your own translations of chosen words. The model has to use them.

A personal dictionary. Add a word and the translation you want, and the model uses it instead of guessing. Useful for company or industry language, names and abbreviations. Entries apply to one language pair only (English to Polish is a different list than German to Polish), and only when the word really appears in what you are translating.
No entries yet. Add a word you want translated your way.
The “%1$s” model will be removed from this phone. Download it again any time over Wi-Fi.
The offline translation models stored on this phone. You do not need both — if you prefer one, the other just takes up space. Tap the bin to delete it; downloading again later is free.
No credits — top up your wallet to use paid models

Which model translates your text when you use the Online engine. The three listed models are hosted by Verbigem and billed to your wallet (best value first). If you paste your own OpenRouter key below, the free “:free” models appear here and translate at no cost to you.
Best value — fast and high quality (~$0.14 / 1M tokens).
Highest quality, regardless of price (~$5 / 1M tokens).
No free models available right now.
No wallet credits — top up your account or add your own OpenRouter key for free models.
Use OpenRouter’s free “:free” models with your own key — translations cost you $0. Get a key at openrouter.ai/keys.

OpenRouter is a service that routes translations to many AI models. Create a free account at openrouter.ai, open the Keys page, and click “Create Key”. Copy the key and paste it here. It is stored only on this phone. Once added, the free “:free” models become available in the online model list above and cost nothing. Generate your key at openrouter.ai/keys.
Balance for paid online models · 1 USD = 1 USD credit
One-time prepaid — hides the ad banner for the chosen period. No subscription.
